approval.trigger: No review or approval of any kind is described before real users can connect: register, get credentials, users authorize. No approval queue, verification step, user cap, or cost appears anywhere in the API docs. Listing is separate and optional: 'To add your application to our public list of Basecamp integrations, go to github.com/basecamp/bc3-integrations and open a pull request' (no criteria, timeline, or fee stated), and nothing ties listing to the ability to connect users.

blockers.detail: The documented authorize URL carries only response_type, client_id, and redirect_uri: no scope parameter, no scope list, no least-privilege selection. The token acts with the authorizing user's full access (Basecamp-issued tokens show a scope field whose example value is 'full'). An agent product cannot down-scope; permission control is whatever the connected user can see and do.
blockers.howToClear: No clearance exists in the Launchpad flow; design your product so its actions stay within what users expect a full-access token to do.
blockers.title: No scopes: authorization is all-or-nothing

flavor.recommended: An OAuth 2 application registered at 37signals Launchpad, standard authorization-code ('web server') flow
flavor.why: 'Register your app at launchpad.37signals.com/integrations. You'll be assigned a client_id and client_secret. You'll need to provide a redirect_uri.' One registration serves every customer: each user authorizes their own Basecamp account. Endpoints: authorize at launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/new, token at launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/token.

humanMust: Register the app at Launchpad and custody the client_secret
Each user authorizes their own Basecamp ID
name: Basecamp
nuances: Two token issuers now exist: Launchpad-issued tokens (the classic flow) and Basecamp-issued tokens; Basecamp serves its own authorization document at 3.basecampapi.com/authorization.json accepting a Basecamp-issued token, a personal access token, or a legacy Launchpad token. Per-account token requests via an RFC 8707 resource parameter (urn:bc:account:<id>) appear in that document.
DPoP exists: a DPoP-bound token authenticates with 'Authorization: DPoP <token>' plus a DPoP proof header, and 'the Bearer scheme is rejected for bound tokens' (RFC 9449).
Mandatory User-Agent: include your app name plus a link or email, or requests fail with 400 Bad Request.

Do NOT build 'Login with Basecamp': the docs warn against using the OAuth API to authenticate users in third-party services because Basecamp doesn't verify email addresses. Also, the identity in the authorization document is 'not used for identifying users within Basecamp'; use the Get person endpoints.

Rate limits are dynamic; the first commonly hit is currently 50 requests per 10 seconds per IP, with Retry-After on 429s. Legacy parameters type=web_server / type=refresh are still accepted but not recommended.
prerequisites: A 37signals/Basecamp ID to sign in to Launchpad
A redirect_uri (a dummy URL is acceptable while building)

steps.detail: Signed in with your 37signals/Basecamp ID, provide the app details and a redirect_uri; you receive client_id and client_secret. The guide notes you may 'enter a dummy URL like http://myapp.com/oauth if you're not ready for this yet'.
steps.title: Register the app at Launchpad

steps.detail: Point your OAuth 2 library at the authorize and token URLs with your client_id, client_secret, and redirect_uri.
steps.title: Configure an OAuth 2 library

steps.detail: Redirect the user to launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/new?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=... 'We authenticate their Basecamp ID and ask whether it's ok to give access to your app.' Basecamp redirects back with a time-limited verification code.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code. Response: access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 1209600 (2 weeks), refresh_token.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: GET launchpad.37signals.com/authorization.json with the bearer token ('This should be the first request after obtaining a user's authorization token'). Pick the account with product 'bc3' and use its href as the base URL; API calls go to 3.basecampapi.com/{account_id}/... Every request needs a User-Agent header with your app name and a link or email, or you get a 400.
steps.title: Discover the account; call the API

steps.detail: POST the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret, on the 2-week cycle per user token.
steps.title: Refresh every 2 weeks

tagline: The simplest serious OAuth in the library: register once at 37signals Launchpad, no review, no scopes at all (the token simply acts as the user), and 2-week access tokens. Listing your app is a GitHub pull request.

time.active: ~5 min of registration + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Same day; nothing stands in front of users
